# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Deception - Interaction With a Decoy Network Service** · `T1046_decoy_service_interaction` · [T1046](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1046_decoy_service_interaction for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     logtype=<value>  node_id=<value>  src_host=<value>
Checked:      1. Confirm node_id is a decoy in deceive/decoys.yml and that no network scan or asset discovery run was declared for the time -> <result>
              2. Resolve src_host to a host and its logged-on user (DHCP lease, 4624 events, EDR) -> <result>
              3. Count the decoy records from that source in the last hour and which services it touched; a login attempt (logtype 2000, 3001, 4002, 6001, 9001) carries the credential it tried in logdata -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | authorised_scanner (applied) | loopback (applied) | monitoring_poller (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Network management or asset discovery tools that sweep every address, when their scanner is not the filtered one
- A new administrator who connects to the decoy because it looks like a real server

Never tune:
- Never filter by destination port or by logtype: the decoy exists to record every service someone touches.
- Never filter a whole subnet: one filtered address is one blind host; a subnet is a blind network.
- Never drop the decoy from the rule without removing it from deceive/decoys.yml; rasd deceive --check fails on the difference.

## Escalation to incident response

```text
Alert:        T1046_decoy_service_interaction for <host> at <time, UTC>
Escalated:    <the condition met, from the list below>
Observed:     logtype=<value>  node_id=<value>  src_host=<value>
Who / where:  <account> on <host>; source <host or address, if any>
Risk:         base 75 + <conditions met> = <score>
Preserved:    The decoy records from the source, in order, with the services and credentials tried -> <where it is saved>
              The source host's process and network telemetry around the first record -> <where it is saved>
              Logons on the source host before the scan -> <where it is saved>
              The decoy's configuration and the inventory entry (which services were enabled when) -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>
Recommended:  Isolate the source host, reset the credentials that were tried if they are real, and keep the decoy running - its log is the evidence
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. The source is a workstation or a server with no network management role
2. A login attempt used a real account name of the organisation
3. Several decoys, or several services of the decoy, were touched from the same source

Risk conditions: outside business hours +10 · host is critical +5 · approved admin activity -40.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Isolate the source host
2. Reset any real credential tried against the decoy
3. Keep the decoy running; record the touch in the deception log
